answer: Entropy provenance. At registration each identity submits a 256-bit pigment from its hardware entropy source plus a TRNG serial; the registry keeps a salted hash and Hamming fingerprint. If two pigments fall within 32 bits, both count as one origin, their umber earnings merge into one capped share, and the newer key must re-register elsewhere. A cipher binding serial to registration nonce blocks replays. Merged shares get audited. A thousand clones from one machine collapse to one share, so farming pays once and loses ninety-nine times.
